title: Lusin's theorem for Lebesgue measure on sets of infinite measure, for Borel maps into L(R^n, R)
statement: Let n be a natural number, L^n = volume on R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n), and L(R^n,R) the finite-dimensional normed space of continuous linear maps R^n -> R with its Borel sigma-algebra. Let F : R^n -> L(R^n,R) be Borel measurable, let S ⊆ R^n be a Borel set (possibly of infinite measure) and let δ ∈ (0, ∞] (an extended nonnegative real with δ ≠ 0). Then there is a closed set C ⊆ S with L^n(S \ C) < δ such that the restriction of F to C is continuous.
lean_statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (F : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] ℝ)), Measurable F → ∀ S : Set (Rn n), MeasurableSet S → ∀ δ : ℝ≥0∞, δ ≠ 0 → ∃ C : Set (Rn n), C ⊆ S ∧ IsClosed C ∧ volume (S \ C) < δ ∧ ContinuousOn F C
